intro: Ignacy Jan Paderewski records Chopin’s Thirds étude in 1923, four years after serving as Poland’s prime minister. The piano part demands fast paired notes in the right hand and a quiet voice.

sections.label: A · Quiet thirds in G♯ minor
sections.mNote: A right-hand trill opens the study, marked sotto voce

sections.label: B · The left hand carries the tune
sections.mNote: A slower melody underpins the quick right-hand thirds

sections.label: C · Paired notes across the keyboard
sections.mNote: Chromatic scales keep the right hand moving in pairs

sections.label: Coda · The last bars of thirds
sections.mNote: The running pairs draw towards the close

cues.title: An undertone at speed
cues.text: Chopin writes sotto voce above one of his most exacting pieces of finger-work. The right hand trills and runs in thirds, two notes sounding together at each step. The left hand’s slower line gives the rushing pairs a melody to accompany.
cues.evidence: Sotto voce and continuous right-hand thirds: https://chopin.nifc.pl/en/chopin/kompozycja/192. Left-hand melody: Fred Yu, https://www.ourchopin.com/analysis/etude25.html.
cues.how: Placed from the score; the timing is approximate.

cues.title: From Warsaw to the piano
cues.text: Cheering crowds greet Paderewski in Warsaw on New Year’s Day 1919. Two weeks later he becomes Poland’s prime minister; that spring he represents the country at the Paris Peace Conference. By February 1920 he returns to his musical career. This Victor recording follows in 1923.
cues.evidence: Andrzej Chojnowski, ‘Paderewski, Ignacy Jan’, 1914–1918-online (2014): Warsaw arrival, 16 January premiership, April peace conference and February 1920 return to music. https://encyclopedia.1914-1918-online.net/article/paderewski-ignacy-jan/. Recording year: https://archive.org/details/78_etude-in-g-sharp-minor_ignace-jan-paderewski-chopin_gbia0183841b.

composer.born: 1 March 1810 by his family’s reckoning; the parish register gives 22 February, Żelazowa Wola, Duchy of Warsaw
composer.epithet: He brought the opera singer’s breath and the mazurka’s wayward accents to a piano that could whisper across a room.
facts: Wojciech Żywny; composition with Józef Elsner in Warsaw, 1826–29
Warsaw · Paris from 1831 · summers at Nohant
Piano lessons, publishing and occasional concerts
The piano, from a few lines of mazurka to concertos and sonatas
composer.background:
In February 1832, a twenty-one-year-old Polish pianist played in the Pleyel rooms in Paris. Chopin had arrived the previous autumn, with two concertos behind him. The concert caught the attention of the city’s publishers; teaching soon supplied his living. He would spend the rest of his life in a profession that depended on people hearing him at close quarters. The great public virtuosos travelled from triumph to triumph. Chopin stayed in Paris and gave lessons.

He was born at Żelazowa Wola in 1810. His father, Nicolas, had come from France and worked as a tutor; his mother, Justyna Krzyżanowska, was Polish. They moved to Warsaw while Fryderyk was still a baby, when Nicolas obtained a teaching post at the Lyceum. At seven the boy already had a polonaise in print. Wojciech Żywny taught him the piano, with Bach and Mozart among his models; Józef Elsner later gave him a rigorous training in composition at Warsaw’s Main School of Music.
